name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Prediction markets price a Democratic win at ~94%
Freshman incumbent with no notable opposition spending
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly Democratic: a 10-point partisan lean, a favorable environment, incumbency, and a dominant money advantage for Olszewski, who has raised over $1 million to Wallace's roughly $20 thousand. Markets price the race around 94% Democratic, consistent with a Safe D call near a 21-point expected margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or unexpected outside spending against Olszewski would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 2nd District sits about ten points to the left of the nation in partisan terms, and first-term Democrat Johnny Olszewski is seeking reelection with the advantages of incumbency in a favorable environment. He has raised more than $1 million and holds over $600,000 in cash, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised about $20,000 with minimal cash on hand and no outside support on either side.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 94%. With no evidence of a competitive race, the district remains safely Democratic, with an expected margin of roughly 21 points and above-average uncertainty given the absence of polling.
